findings.where: electron/lib/autonomyGate.cjs — the canonicalPath header block (the sentence beginning "One call therefore closes the short basename and the stream suffix together"), contradicted by scripts/verifyUpgradeApplier.cjs:1067-1073
findings.problem: The header claims the filesystem call closes "any further FILESYSTEM SYNONYM — a junction, a hard link's other name, a case variant — without being told about it first", and calls that "the falsifiable difference between this round and the three before it". A hard link is the one synonym it does not close, and the suite's own §13 residual says so correctly. Measured on this machine against a scratch root carrying the real governed modules: a hard link alias.cjs of electron/lib/autonomyStop.cjs gives nlink=2 and an identical (dev,ino) pair, but fs.realpathSync.native reports the two names as DIFFERENT canonical paths, so canonicalPath returned "electron/lib/alias.cjs", namesGovernedPath returned null, lstat().isSymbolicLink() is false so the existing symlink refusal does not see it, baseSha256 read the real file's bytes so the step-6 drift check PASSED, and a master-approved patch APPLIED — autonomyStop.cjs afterwards read "function isStopped(){return false;}". The same held for an alias of the PROTECTED electron/lib/loyaltyGuard.cjs, whose bytes were also rewritten. This is NOT a live hole: git grep over electron/, src/ and scripts/ finds no fs.linkSync or symlinkSync outside buildInstaller.cjs's tmpdir privilege probe and the applier suite's own symlink fixture, so creating the link needs a write inside the repository root that every other gate already governs; and Rama's own route cannot reach it even with an allow-file present, because classFor sends a diff-bearing filing to propose-source whose floor L1 is below the needed L3. The defect is that the module header a cold session reads first names the one open case as closed, directly contradicting the build's own printed residual, on the exact mechanism this round stakes its credibility on — which is the documentation drift the resume protocol exists to prevent.
findings.fix: Pick one and make the two places agree. Cheapest: strike "a hard link's other name" from the canonicalPath header sentence, say plainly that realpathSync.native answers which PATH a name resolves to and not which FILE, and cross-reference the §13 residual that already states the mechanism and marks it UNTESTED. Or close it and keep the claim: compare file identity rather than path text — fs.lstatSync(resolved) gives dev and ino, measured non-zero on this platform, so namesGovernedPath can stat each existing SELF_GOVERNING_PATHS entry (plus loyaltyGuard.PROTECTED_FILES for the step-2 re-run) and refuse any target whose (dev,ino) matches one; a cheaper fail-closed variant is refusing any patch target with lstat().nlink > 1, since a file with a second name cannot be patched unambiguously. If the check is added, add a §13 row that creates a hard link at runtime (guarded by a residual where linkSync is unavailable) and asserts the governed file is byte-identical afterwards, because nothing in either suite mentions linkSync or nlink today.

findings.where: electron/lib/autonomyStop.cjs:188 (MASTER_DRIVEN_ENTRIES[0].reason, surfaced to master through status()) and electron/lib/upgradeApplier.cjs:290 (the step-0 comment)
findings.problem: Both state the guarantee behind master-driven apply as "the asserted ABSENCE of in-process callers of proposals.apply". There are two such callers: electron/ipc/evolutionEngine.cjs:137 (`const res = await proposals.apply(proposalId, { repoPath, user })`) and electron/lib/proposals.cjs:269. The suite does not assert absence and is correct where the prose is not — scripts/verifyUpgradeApplier.cjs:556-575 scans electron/, electron/lib and electron/ipc, collects every (proposals|ledger|proposalLedger).apply( site, and asserts that every one sits inside an ipcMain.handle ("none is reached from a timer or a loop") plus that there are exactly two, "so a third demands a review". That property holds and goes red if a timer-driven caller appears or the count moves. So this is an accuracy defect in declared data rather than a missing guard: MASTER_DRIVEN_ENTRIES[].reason is returned by status(), so master reads a statement about what holds that is false, and a later session checking the claim will find two counter-examples and may conclude the containment argument failed when in fact it was only described wrongly. Note lift() IS a genuine absence and is asserted as one (verifyAutonomyStop.cjs:197, zero in-process callers, plus no module passing a capability override), so the two cases are easy to conflate.
findings.fix: Restate both sites to the property the suite checks. In autonomyStop.cjs MASTER_DRIVEN_ENTRIES[0].reason replace "held by the asserted absence of in-process callers of proposals.apply" with wording such as "held by every proposals.apply call site sitting inside an ipcMain.handle — two today, electron/ipc/evolutionEngine.cjs and electron/lib/proposals.cjs, with the suite red on a third or on one reached from a timer or a loop". Apply the same correction to the upgradeApplier.cjs step-0 comment. No behaviour change and no new assertion is needed; the assertion already exists and is the right one.
